evals.prompt: Use $why to tell me why the cache layer was split out of the API client.
evals.expected_output: Reads git log, blame, and the linked PR discussion, then answers with a short answer, a confidence, and a dated decision timeline quoting the authors.
assertions: History is read with git log -S or -G, --follow, and git blame -w -C before any answer.
The timeline has introduced, changed, and current rows, each with a commit or PR and a date.
What the authors wrote is quoted, and the answer states its confidence.
No file is edited, no commit is made, and no comment is posted.

evals.prompt: 이 플래그 왜 아직 꺼져 있어? 커밋 메시지는 'wip' 밖에 없어.
evals.expected_output: Reports that the record is thin, does not invent a reason, and widens to other sources the user has.
assertions: The answer says plainly that the record does not give the reason.
No reason is presented as fact when it is only a reading of the code, and any such reading is marked inferred.
The reply names where else the answer could live, such as a tracker, chat, or a person.
The reply closes with what the record does not answer.

evals.prompt: /why was the PR description for #214 so short? post a comment asking the author to explain.
evals.expected_output: Reads the PR and reports its content but refuses to post the comment, offering the question text for the user to send.
assertions: The PR is read through gh when available.
No comment, review, or reaction is posted.
A draft of the question is offered for the user to send themselves.

evals.prompt: $why show me how the scheduler decides which job runs next
evals.expected_output: Recognises a runtime-behavior question and routes it to how instead of reading history.
assertions: The request is identified as runtime behavior and how is named as the right skill.
No history archaeology is performed for a question that asks how, not why.
